entry.name: process-exec-scrub-cloexec
entry.title: tests(process): pin exec_scrub cloexec-only teardown and pipe release
entry.body:
### What
Pins `exec_scrub`: only cloexec ends are closed, their pipes released, surviving fds stay usable, and the call is idempotent.

### Why it matters
exec must drop cloexec descriptors without touching kept ones. No existing test exercises exec_scrub, so inverting the cloexec predicate or miscounting survives.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| `entry.cloexec` -> `!entry.cloexec` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| return `0` instead of `count` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-process --lib exec_scrub_drops`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.

entry.body:

Pins that an unlinked overlay slot is scrubbed (data zeroed, len reset) before reuse so a fresh overlay never leaks prior bytes.

### Why it matters

entry.name: process-retain-refcount
entry.title: tests(process): pin duplicate retain counts and source-close survival

mutants.name: noop-retain
decrement-retain

entry.body:
### What
Pins `retain` via duplicate: both duplicated ends raise the count to 4, closing originals keeps the pipe alive, only the last copy frees it.

### Why it matters
Over-retaining leaks pipe objects; skipping the increment retains nothing and under-counts duplicates. Existing duplicate tests pin single-end retention, not both-ends survival.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| no-op retain (early return) | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| decrement instead of increment | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-process --lib duplicate_retains`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.

reason: covered: existing pipe_release_frees_only_after_last_end (@2105-2121) pins exact retain counts after duplicate/close; every public-API retain mutant (noop/decrement/+N) is killed by it; live-check unreachable via duplicate lookup guard

entry.name: process-unshare-copy
entry.title: tests(process): pin unshare private-copy, solo no-op, and unknown-task edges
entry.body:
### What
Pins `unshare`: a shared descriptor table is copied privately (pipe ends retained), a solo task is a no-op, and unknown tasks return Ok without allocation.

### Why it matters
Exec unshares files before CLOEXEC scrub; counting zero members or off-by-one on the member threshold either leaks shared fds across exec or double-retains pipes. No existing test exercises unshare.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| `**member != 0` -> `== 0` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| `> 1` -> `>= 1` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-process --lib unshare_copies_shared`.

entry.name: kernel-views-cgroup-remove-busy
entry.title: tests(kernel-views): pin cgroup remove busy guard for active children
entry.body:
### What
Pins `remove` busy semantics: an active child group blocks parent removal, leaf groups remove cleanly, freed inactive slots never block, root and non-root callers are denied.

### Why it matters
The busy guard chains `active && path != self && parent == path`; flipping any operator lets parents of live children be removed (orphaning confinement) or blocks legitimate cleanup. Existing tests pin only the member-count branch.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| `group.active &&` -> `group.active ||` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| `parent_path(...) == path` -> `!= path` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-kernel-views --lib remove_busy_only`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.

entry.name: vfs-decode-boundary-exact
entry.title: tests(vfs): pin decode_record exact path/link bounds and overflow rejection
entry.body:
### What
Pins `decode_record` length gates: exact MAX_PATH/MAX_LINK fit decodes, one-past-MAX_LINK and zero-length path are rejected at index load.

### Why it matters
Decode gates guard every record read; relaxing `>` to `>=` rejects valid exact-fit images, while `==` admits oversized links that later slice out of bounds. Existing tests pin encode-side and path-overflow only, not decode-side exact fit or link overflow.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| `link_len > MAX_LINK` -> `>=` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| `path_len > MAX_PATH` -> `==` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-vfs --lib decode_record_accepts_exact`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.

entry.name: process-event-poll-admission
entry.title: tests(process): pin EventPoll add admission for zero, invalid mask, and duplicates
entry.body:
### What
Pins `EventPoll::add` admission: descriptor 0, zero events, unsupported mask bits, and duplicate active descriptors are rejected; valid single/combined masks accepted; freed slots reusable.

### Why it matters
Admission gates prevent invalid poll registrations that corrupt readiness reporting. Flipping `||` to `&&` admits zero-descriptor entries; XOR instead of AND-NOT misvalidates the event mask. Existing tests exercise only the happy path.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| first `||` -> `&&` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| `& !(...)` -> `^ (...)` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-process --lib event_poll_add_rejects`.

### Why it matters

entry.name: devices-random-xorshift
entry.title: tests(devices): pin Random read xorshift64 sequence and state advancement
entry.body:
### What
Pins `DeviceRegistry::read` Random xorshift64 sequence: first four bytes match the reference algorithm from default seed, and successive reads advance state.

### Why it matters
The PRNG drives /dev/random output; replacing XOR with OR or flipping shift direction produces a degenerate or predictable stream. Existing tests verify read succeeds but never pin output values.

| `^= ... << 13` -> `\|= ... << 13` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| `<< 13` -> `>> 13` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-devices --lib random_read_pins`.
